subtopics.title: Why Atoms Bond, and the Lewis Diagram Toolkit

questions.question: Two hydrogen atoms bond while two helium atoms do not because:
options: Hydrogen atoms are lighter than helium atoms
Sharing electrons lowers the energy of hydrogen atoms, but helium's filled shell gains nothing from sharing
Helium atoms repel all other atoms
Hydrogen atoms carry opposite charges

questions.question: On the potential energy versus distance graph for two hydrogen atoms, the bond length corresponds to:
options: The distance where the energy curve is steepest
The largest distance on the graph
The distance at the minimum of the energy curve
The distance where the energy is zero

questions.question: In the Lewis diagram of ammonia, nitrogen has:
options: Three bonding pairs and one lone pair
Four bonding pairs and no lone pairs
Two bonding pairs and two lone pairs
One bonding pair and three lone pairs

questions.question: A dative covalent bond, as in the hydronium ion, is one in which:
options: The electrons are transferred completely
Each atom contributes one electron
Three pairs are shared at once
One atom supplies both electrons of the shared pair

questions.question: Electron pairs around a central atom arrange themselves:
options: As close together as possible
As far apart as possible, because they repel one another
In whatever pattern the drawing shows
Randomly

questions.question: Methane's four bonding pairs give it the shape of a:
options: Flat square with 90° angles
Straight line
Tetrahedron with angles of 109,5°
Triangle with 120° angles

questions.question: Water has four electron pairs around oxygen, yet its shape is called angular because:
options: The shape is named after the atoms only, and two of the pairs are lone pairs
Two of its electrons are missing
Oxygen refuses the tetrahedral arrangement
The hydrogen atoms repel each other into a line

questions.question: The bond angle shrinks from 109,5° in methane to about 104,5° in water because:
options: Water has fewer electrons in total
Oxygen is smaller than carbon
Water's bonds are shorter
Lone pairs repel more strongly than bonding pairs and squeeze the bonds together

subtopics.title: Electronegativity and the Polarity of Bonds

questions.question: Electronegativity is defined as:
options: The charge on an ion
A measure of an atom's tendency to attract the shared electron pair in a bond
The energy needed to remove an electron
The number of valence electrons an atom has

questions.question: In hydrogen chloride (H: 2,1; Cl: 3,0), the chlorine end of the bond is:
options: δ+, because chlorine is bigger
Neutral
δ−, because chlorine attracts the shared pair more strongly
Positively ionised

questions.question: A bond between two identical atoms, like H–H, is always:
options: Non-polar covalent, because the electronegativity difference is zero
Polar covalent
Ionic
Dative

questions.question: Sodium chloride (Na: 0,9; Cl: 3,0) is classified as ionic because:
options: Both atoms share the pair equally
The molecules are very large
Sodium attracts electrons strongly
The electronegativity difference of 2,1 is large enough for complete electron transfer

subtopics.title: Polar Molecules, Bond Energy and Bond Length

questions.question: Carbon dioxide contains polar bonds but is a non-polar molecule because:
options: Its linear shape makes the two equal bond dipoles cancel exactly
Its bonds are actually non-polar
Oxygen and carbon have equal electronegativities
The molecule is too small to be polar

questions.question: Water IS a polar molecule because:
options: Its bonds are stronger than carbon dioxide's
Its angular shape stops the two bond dipoles from cancelling
It contains more hydrogen atoms
Oxygen is a large atom

questions.question: Comparing carbon-carbon single, double and triple bonds:
options: The single bond is the shortest and strongest
All three have the same length
The triple bond is the shortest and strongest
The double bond is longer than the single bond

questions.question: Going down a group, bonds between those atoms and hydrogen generally become:
options: Shorter and stronger
Shorter and weaker
Longer and stronger
Longer and weaker, because larger atoms bond at greater distances

questions.question: In the energy-valley picture, atoms bond because:
options: Rolling into the valley lowers their energy
They are attracted to warmth
The valley pushes them apart
Higher energy is more stable

questions.question: The depth of the energy valley represents:
options: The bond length
The bond energy — how hard the pair is to separate
The number of shared electrons
The size of the atoms

questions.question: In a Lewis diagram, a lone pair is drawn as:
options: A pair of dots between two atoms
A single dot far from any atom
A pair of dots resting on its own atom, not shared with another
A line connecting three atoms

questions.question: Four balloons tied at their necks spring into a tetrahedron because:
options: Balloons naturally form squares
Gravity pulls them downward
The knot forces that shape
Each balloon pushes the others as far away as possible

questions.question: Ammonia is described as pyramidal rather than tetrahedral because:
options: One of its four electron pairs is a lone pair, and shapes are named after visible atoms only
It only has three electron pairs in total
Nitrogen cannot form tetrahedra
Its bonds are double bonds

questions.question: The flat cross drawn for methane in a workbook is:
options: The molecule's true shape
A two-dimensional shadow of the real tetrahedral shape
Wrong — methane is linear
Only correct at high temperatures

questions.question: In the tug-of-war picture, electronegativity is:
options: The length of the rope
The number of players
Each atom's pulling strength on the shared electrons
The referee

questions.question: The slide from covalent to ionic bonding is best described as:
options: A smooth gradient from fair sharing through unfair sharing to complete taking, marked by the electronegativity difference
A sudden jump at a difference of exactly 1,0
Two completely unrelated types of bonding
A change that only happens when molecules melt

questions.question: A molecule with polar bonds is non-polar overall when:
options: It contains fewer than three atoms
It is dissolved in water
Its bonds are all single bonds
Its shape makes the bond pulls cancel exactly, as in linear carbon dioxide

questions.question: Water's bent shape matters because it:
options: Makes the molecule lighter
Stops the bond pulls from cancelling, leaving the molecule polar
Allows the molecule to stack neatly
Cancels the pull of both hydrogens
